effective.acceptance: The report's trace table has one row per requirement of the Mantle specification's Appendix (each gas table entry, the ZkSignature definition, multi-Ed25519 verification, the proof of claim definition, each test vector), in the document's order, each with a file:line in the unit or an explicit 'not in unit' / 'needs external evidence'. Every confirmed code finding has a new test in logos-blockchain-core, logos-blockchain-zksign or logos-blockchain-poc that fails on 0.3.0 for the divergence it names. Prose-only findings are marked as such. The target implementation is unchanged.
effective.context:
Logos Blockchain is a Rust workspace (edition 2024, toolchain 1.99.0 pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, Cargo.lock committed). Package names carry a `logos-blockchain-` prefix the directory names lack; the `name` field of each crate's Cargo.toml is authoritative. The audited ref is the release tag 0.3.0 (commit 1da2d9d69a80452cf6b5d0e68304762d510c8a6c); record the resolved commit in the report. The specification in the prompt is one section of the Bedrock v1.1 Mantle specification LIP as published in the logos-lips repository at commit fddc2c1 (the 2026-10-08 Bedrock snapshot).

The Appendix holds gas determination (the per-operation gas table and its derivation), the Zero Knowledge Signature Scheme (ZkSignature) and its benchmark, multiple Ed25519 signature verification, the Proof of Claim and its benchmark, and the Test Vectors (operation id, Mantle transaction hash, declaration id). Its requirements are the gas values, the signature scheme's inputs and verification rule, and every test vector's exact bytes; benchmark figures are informative, not requirements.

Where the Appendix lives in the code:
- core/src/mantle/gas.rs and src/mantle/transactions/gas.rs (package `logos-blockchain-core`): the gas constants and the per-operation gas computation. src/mantle/transactions/hash.rs and src/mantle/fixtures/hash.rs: the transaction hash and its fixtures, where the test vectors should be reproduced. src/mantle/ops/proof_zk_and_ed.rs: the combined ZkSignature and Ed25519 proof and how multiple Ed25519 signatures are verified. src/proofs/leader_claim_proof.rs: the proof of claim public inputs. src/sdp/mod.rs: the declaration id.
- zk/proofs/zksign/src (package `logos-blockchain-zksign`): the ZkSignature scheme: inputs.rs, public.rs, private.rs, witness.rs, verification_key/, lib.rs. zk/proofs/poc/src (package `logos-blockchain-poc`): the proof of claim bindings. Both circuits are prebuilt crates (feature `prebuilt`); what they constrain is 'needs external evidence'.

Running tests: the gate runs the unit's packages with cargo-nextest, which is what CI uses (`.github/workflows/code-check.yml` runs the whole workspace that way; the whole workspace is too large for this container, so the gate is narrowed to the unit). `cargo nextest run --locked -p <package> --all-features` runs one package; `cargo test --locked -p <package> --all-features -- <filter>` works too. `.config/nextest.toml` marks a unit test slow after 30 s and kills it after 2 min. ZK proof dependencies come as prebuilt circuit crates (`lbc-*-sys` with the `prebuilt` feature) and the verifier links rapidsnark statically, so the first build compiles C++ and takes a while; nothing needs a running node, docker, or downloaded circuit files. New proof tests go in the owning crate's tests/ directory or as a `#[cfg(test)]` module file under src/ named by finding id; the Test Vectors are the natural source of exact-value proofs. Treat code comments that cite a spec paragraph as claims to check.
